note:
Re-recorded once for the five demo changes that landed together: bind-a-value-an-entry-did-not-generate, answer-a-machine-question-as-a-record, show-a-deployment-in-a-browser, author-a-deployment-from-outside and enroll-a-friend-outside-the-harness. Two facts of that set are evaluated here, and both are in `lib/**`.

1. author-a-deployment-from-outside publishes the authoring vocabulary from the library - `lib/vocabulary.nix` plus `moduleKeys` in `lib/module.nix` and the four registry key lists in `lib/resolve.nix`. Whole-evaluation delta, constant at every fixture and every size: nrThunks +1, values.number +1, sets.bytes +96, envs.bytes +16, nothing else. Publishing an attribute allocates its slot, once per library import rather than per plan entry, so the figure shrinks with fleet size, and the slot is the cheapest implementation of a published value.

2. `dedup` in `lib/diagnostics.nix` now discards the string context of the key it builds from a row's own text. This is a totality fix rather than a refactor: an attribute name may carry no context, a row's message may name a store path - a closure root nothing mentions is one - and `mkPlan` therefore ended the evaluation inside the table that exists to report it, which is the invariant that `lib/` never raises. `tests/counterexamples/probes.nix`'s `aRowNamingAStorePathIsStillARow` is the pin. One discard at the one key is the cheapest implementation that holds: the same discard inside `util.oneLine` runs three to four times per row and measured 45 figures over budget against this one's 33, at `worked` gc.totalBytes 61794.9091 against 61410.9091, so the key alone is what is recorded. Discarding at the farms' writes cannot replace it, because the failing use is a key and not a file; `operator/default.nix` discards there as well, and that half costs no gated counter because `perf/eval.nix` plans and never builds.

Across both, the largest per-entry move is 0.11% (`worked` nrPrimOpCalls), gc.totalBytes moves in both directions, and nrOpUpdateValuesCopied and list.elements do not move at any fixture - nothing landed inside a per-plan or per-machine update. The prediction of byte-identical counters in openspec/changes/author-a-deployment-from-outside/tasks.md task 1.1 and in openspec/changes/INTEGRATION.md is corrected there against this measurement.

growth.note: The bound applies to every fixture measured at more than one size, and it is 1.25 because the cost per plan entry has to stay flat as the fleet grows: `fleet` grows the number of entries and keeps each entry's own work constant, `mesh` grows one entry's work with the fleet and keeps the plan linear in it, and a quarter of slack absorbs constant-factor noise without admitting any super-linear term.
